Barnstars

Geography Barnstar ---- I User:Bjrobinson, whether I am meant to or not, hereby award with the 'Geography Barnstar' for your long term, tireless and continuously high quality edits to places in the UK, and especially Bristol. You sir, are an example to us all, and I thank you on behalf of everyone on the entire planet with internet access. Bjrobinson 14:40, 16 May 2007 (UTC)

== Specific epithet ''handseni'' or ''hanseni''? ==

IRMNG gives ''handseni'' but other RS use ''hanseni''. e.g.
*[https://www.eu-nomen.eu/portal/taxon.php?GUID=urn:lsid:faunaeur.org:taxname:85033 Fauna Europaea]
*[https://treatment.plazi.org/GgServer/html/03C08371CC55FF9CBDBC2077FED7FEA3 Plazi]
*[https://www.gbif.org/species/4513717 GBIF] (which gives its source as Fauna Europaea)
*[https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/3458613361 A specimen labelled "Typus" in red]

Citation for original publication given by Plazi is "Entomologiske Meddelelser, 22 (2): 140".
: [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 14:18, 17 January 2026 (UTC)

== Latin gender ==

In "Description of advanced third-stage larvae of Gnathostoma lamothei Bertoni-Ruiz et al. 2005 (Nematoda: Gnathostomatidae) from experimental hosts and contributions to its life cycle", a paper subsequent to the one cited here, this species is referred to as ''Gnathostoma sociale''. This because "stoma" has neuter gender in Latin. (In the case of ''G. procyonis'', "procyonis", meaning "of the racoon", is the genitive of the masculine noun ''[[Procyon (genus)|Procyon]]''.) So this page should be moved to ''Gnathostoma sociale'', the name given in WoRMS. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 07:33, 31 January 2026 (UTC)

:I find Station1's point about using "former" to be at best captious, and probably outright wrong through overzealous application of logic to language. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 15:32, 10 March 2026 (UTC)

* '''Support'''  – Looking at [[:Category:Beatifications]] and its subcategories, I could only spot [[Beatification of Pope John Paul II]] as a standalone article on a beatification. I realise that we can have articles on any subject with reliable sources, but what makes it necessary in this case? The existing article on Popiełuszko is not overly long. Similar considerations must apply to the canonisation. Where there is a substantial article about the person, and the canonisation process has controversial aspects, as with [[John Henry Newman]], I can see the point, but at the moment there's no reason for a standalone article in this case. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 13:41, 15 March 2026 (UTC)

== Etymology in lead ==

I am of the opinion that etymology should generally be kept out of lead sections, on the grounds that Wikipedia is an encyclopedia, not a dictionary. It is also incorrect to delete cited material from the article body and insert it, with citation, into the lead. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 07:38, 3 April 2026 (UTC)

'''Being involved in an edit war can result in you being [[Wikipedia:Blocking policy|blocked from editing]]'''—especially if you violate the [[Wikipedia:Edit warring#The three-revert rule|three-revert rule]], which states that an editor must not perform more than three [[Help:Reverting|reverts]] on a single page within a 24-hour period.  Undoing another editor's work—whether in whole or in part, whether involving the same or different material each time—counts as a revert.  Also keep in mind that while violating the three-revert rule often leads to a block, you can still be blocked for edit warring—'''even if you do not violate the three-revert rule'''—should your behavior indicate that you intend to continue reverting repeatedly.<!-- Template:uw-3rr --> [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 19:46, 27 March 2025 (UTC)

== Nomination of [[:Oxalis rusciformis]] for deletion ==
[[File:Ambox warning orange.svg|48px|alt=|link=]]
A discussion is taking place as to whether the article [[:Oxalis rusciformis]] is suitable for inclusion in Wikipedia according to [[Wikipedia:List of policies and guidelines|Wikipedia's policies and guidelines]] or whether it should be [[Wikipedia:Deletion policy|deleted]]. The article will be discussed at '''[[Wikipedia:Articles for deletion/Oxalis rusciformis]]''' until a consensus is reached, and anyone, including you, is welcome to contribute to the discussion. The nomination will explain the policies and guidelines which are of concern. The discussion focuses on high-quality evidence and our policies and guidelines. For a subject exclusively related to the United Kingdom (for example, a famous British person), use [[British English]]. For something related to the United States in the same way, use [[American English]]. For something related to another [[List of countries and territories where English is an official language|English-speaking country]], such as Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, India, or Pakistan, use the variety of English used there. For an international topic, use the form of English that the ''first'' author of the article used.

In view of that, please don't change articles from one version of English to another, even if you don't normally use the version in which the article is written. Respect other people's versions of English. They, in turn, should respect yours. Other general guidelines on how Wikipedia articles are written can be found in the [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style|Manual of Style]]. == National varieties of English ==

[[File:Information.svg|25px|alt=Information icon]] Hello. In a recent edit to the page [[:Finnegans Wake]], you changed one or more words or styles from one national variety of English to another. Because Wikipedia has readers from all over the world, our policy is to [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style#National varieties of English|respect national varieties of English]] in Wikipedia articles.

For a subject exclusively related to the United Kingdom (for example, a famous British person), use [[British English]]. For something related to the United States in the same way, use [[American English]]. For something related to another [[List of countries and territories where English is an official language|English-speaking country]], such as Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, India, or Pakistan, use the variety of English used there. For an international topic, use the form of English that the ''first'' author of the article used.

In view of that, please don't change articles from one version of English to another, even if you don't normally use the version in which the article is written. Respect other people's versions of English. They, in turn, should respect yours. Other general guidelines on how Wikipedia articles are written can be found in the [[Wikipedia:Manual of Style|Manual of Style]]. If you have any questions about this, you can ask me on [[User talk:William Avery|my talk page]] or visit the [[Wikipedia:Help desk|help desk]]. items.post_text:
== Specific epithet ''handseni'' or ''hanseni''? ==

IRMNG gives ''handseni'' but other RS use ''hanseni''. e.g.
*[https://www.eu-nomen.eu/portal/taxon.php?GUID=urn:lsid:faunaeur.org:taxname:85033 Fauna Europaea]
*[https://treatment.plazi.org/GgServer/html/03C08371CC55FF9CBDBC2077FED7FEA3 Plazi]
*[https://www.gbif.org/species/4513717 GBIF] (which gives its source as Fauna Europaea)
*[https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/3458613361 A specimen labelled "Typus" in red]

Citation for original publication given by Plazi is "Entomologiske Meddelelser, 22 (2): 140".
: [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 14:18, 17 January 2026 (UTC)

== Latin gender ==

In "Description of advanced third-stage larvae of Gnathostoma lamothei Bertoni-Ruiz et al. 2005 (Nematoda: Gnathostomatidae) from experimental hosts and contributions to its life cycle", a paper subsequent to the one cited here, this species is referred to as ''Gnathostoma sociale''. This because "stoma" has neuter gender in Latin. (In the case of ''G. procyonis'', "procyonis", meaning "of the racoon", is the genitive of the masculine noun ''[[Procyon (genus)|Procyon]]''.) So this page should be moved to ''Gnathostoma sociale'', the name given in WoRMS. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 07:33, 31 January 2026 (UTC)

* '''Support'''  – Looking at [[:Category:Beatifications]] and its subcategories, I could only spot [[Beatification of Pope John Paul II]] as a standalone article on a beatification. I realise that we can have articles on any subject with reliable sources, but what makes it necessary in this case? The existing article on Popiełuszko is not overly long. Similar considerations must apply to the canonisation. Where there is a substantial article about the person, and the canonisation process has controversial aspects, as with [[John Henry Newman]], I can see the point, but at the moment there's no reason for a standalone article in this case. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 13:41, 15 March 2026 (UTC)

:Articles about living people need to be based on reliable secondary sources. See [[WP:BLPPRIMARY]]. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 19:48, 18 January 2025 (UTC)

== Etymology in lead ==

I am of the opinion that etymology should generally be kept out of lead sections, on the grounds that Wikipedia is an encyclopedia, not a dictionary. It is also incorrect to delete cited material from the article body and insert it, with citation, into the lead. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 07:38, 3 April 2026 (UTC)

== Latin gender ==

In "Description of advanced third-stage larvae of Gnathostoma lamothei Bertoni-Ruiz et al. 2005 (Nematoda: Gnathostomatidae) from experimental hosts and contributions to its life cycle", a paper subsequent to the one cited here, this species is referred to as ''Gnathostoma sociale''. This because "stoma" has neuter gender in Latin. (In the case of ''G. procyonis'', "procyonis", meaning "of the racoon", is the genitive of the masculine noun ''[[Procyon (genus)|Procyon]]''.) So this page should be moved to ''Gnathostoma sociale'', the name given in WoRMS. [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 07:33, 31 January 2026 (UTC)

== Ameripodius alexis ==

A second species of ''Ameripodius'', ''A. alexis'', has been described. See https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.0031-0239.2000.00136.x [[User:William Avery|William Avery]] ([[User talk:William Avery|talk]]) 09:03, 10 March 2025 (UTC)

* '''Support'''  – Looking at [[:Category:Beatifications]] and its subcategories, I could only spot [[Beatification of Pope John Paul II]] as a standalone article on a beatification. I realise that we can have articles on any subject with reliable sources, but what makes it necessary in this case? The existing article on Popiełuszko is not overly long. Similar considerations must apply to the canonisation. Where there is a substantial article about the person, and the canonisation process has controversial aspects, as with [[John Henry Newman]], I can see the point, but at the moment there's no reason for a standalone article in this case.
